candidates: In diagram Jison parsers, keep the grammar lean by accepting style definitions as a single raw string token rather than parsing individual style properties within the grammar rules; delegate all style string parsing and validation to the JavaScript DB layer. Follow the approach used in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/flowchart/parser/flow.jison` as the canonical reference.

When validating user-provided style property names or values in diagram parsers, throw an explicit, named error (e.g., a custom `Error` subclass such as `InvalidStyleError`) rather than silently ignoring the value or logging a warning.

New parsing or validation utility functions must have dedicated unit tests covering: valid input with all supported parameters, empty/missing input, unsupported property names, and each distinct category of invalid value format (e.g., bad hex code, non-numeric value, missing unit suffix).

In Cypress `imgSnapshotTest` calls that use template literals, ensure the closing backtick and closing parenthesis are each on their own correctly-indented line; misplaced closures cause subtle syntax or argument-passing bugs.
Use TypeScript interface `extends` and `Pick<>` to compose new interfaces from existing base types rather than redeclaring fields that already exist in those types.

Provide explicit type annotations on class field declarations, especially when the field is initialized with an empty object or array literal (`= {}`), so the intended shape is unambiguous without requiring inference.

Extract validation helper functions (hex color format, pixel-size format, integer checks, etc.) into a dedicated `utils.ts` module rather than inlining them in the DB or service layer; this keeps the DB layer focused and makes validators independently testable and reusable.
Use `for...of` loops for array iteration instead of manual length checks combined with `forEach`; this reduces nesting, is idiomatic TypeScript, and is the preferred style in this codebase.
Use strict equality operators (`===` and `!==`) instead of abstract equality (`==` and `!=`) throughout the codebase — this is a project-wide convention.

When building rendered data objects from raw input points, apply the `point.property || themeDefault` fallback pattern consistently for all overridable style properties; do not apply it to some properties while hardcoding defaults for others.

Parser tests should include inputs with varying amounts of whitespace around delimiters (commas, colons, between tokens) to verify that the parser handles whitespace robustly, not just the canonical single-space form.

Expected error message strings in unit tests must exactly match the messages produced by the source code's error constructors; cross-check them character-for-character against the actual constructor arguments to avoid false-passing tests.
